subject: Proof of EU node presence, keystore controls, and VPC inventory
messages:
From: Lena Martell <lena.martell@evergreenhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <ops@datasecure.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Request: Affirmation of EU node, keystore & VPC inventory

Hi Sean —

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SIG + CAIQ review we need concise, auditable evidence that Redwood is currently running inference nodes in the EU region that are logically separate from US tenancy, and that the keystore handling for EU workloads is scoped to EU-only key material (or clearly documented KMS partitioning). In addition, our security team requires a short VPC/private-link inventory showing peering endpoints, IP ranges, and the operator contact list for any private deployments that could touch our traffic.

Can you provide: 
- A one-page statement confirming EU node presence and tenancy boundaries (suitable for inclusion in our SIG response).
- Keystore/rotation summary for EU material (high level; we only need controls + rotation cadence and who has access).
- VPC/Privatelink inventory (endpoints, CIDR ranges, peering owners).
- Any SOC 2/CAIQ excerpts that specifically reference region separation or key management.

We'd appreciate the packet by EOD tomorrow (Wed 15 Jul). If anything needs an internal redaction, flag it.

Best,
Lena
Head of InfoSec, Evergreen Health

---
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Lena Martell <lena.martell@evergreenhealth.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <ops@datasecure.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: Affirmation of EU node, keystore & VPC inventory

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. Quick notes: 
- We do run dedicated inference capacity in eu-west-1 for customers who require EU residency (separate ASE/tenant logical boundaries).
- Keystore: EU workloads can be configured to use a customer-specific KMS key in the EU region; application-level key material for system-managed keys is rotated on a 90-day cadence.
- I'll coordinate a small packet that combines a short declaration + the inventory CSV you asked for.

Looping in our infra and compliance leads to assemble the artifacts by EOD tomorrow.

Sean
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 19:05:00 +0000
Subject: FW: Request: Affirmation of EU node, keystore & VPC inventory

Sean — short runbook for what I'll attach: 
1) redwood-eu-node-inventory-2026-07.csv (columns: node_id, region, AZ, tenant_tag, instance_type, public_eip=false, private_cidr, owner_oncall)
2) privatelink-topology-diagram.png (visual, shows privatelink endpoints per account)
3) keystore-rotation-summary.pdf (exported from KMS ops; includes rotation cadence, access ACL roles, and HSM usage note)
4) soc2-snapshot-2026.pdf (excerpt pages referencing logical separation & KMS controls)

Irene/Grace: can you verify operator contacts in column owner_oncall? I pulled last known from our oncall roster but want to be sure before sharing externally.

Karthik
Senior Infra Eng

---
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Lena Martell <lena@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <ops@datasecure.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:43:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: Affirmation of EU node, keystore & VPC inventory

Lena / Daniel — attached is the packet we discussed. Highlights:
- Affirmation: Redwood operates a logical tenancy partition for EU-resident workloads (we can provide an operator-run trace of control plane tenancy on request). The eu-west-1 inference pool is not co-located with US tenant pools; network egress for EU-flagged workloads is routed via EU-only subnets.
- Keystore: EU key material is scoped to EU KMS keys; system-managed keys follow a 90-day rotation, HSM-backed where required for enterprise plans. Access is limited to RBAC roles listed in keystore-rotation-summary.pdf.
- VPC Inventory: See CSV for endpoints and owner_oncall contact. PrivateLink endpoints show dedicated peering to customer VPCs where enabled — we list IP ranges and the responsible SRE.

Files attached: redwood-eu-node-inventory-2026-07.csv, keystore-rotation-summary.pdf, privatelink-topology-diagram.png, soc2-snapshot-2026.pdf

If you want a signed letter on company letterhead stating the residency commitment, we can prepare one — please tell us what level of signature or notarization you need.

Regards,
Sean

---
From: Lena Martell <lena.martell@evergreenhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <ops@datasecure.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: Affirmation of EU node, keystore & VPC inventory

Sean — received the packet, thank you. The inventory CSV and keystore summary look good. A couple of quick follow-ups: 
- Can you confirm whether any scheduled cross-region backups (snapshots) contain EU customer secrets and where those snapshots are stored? 
- For the SOC 2 excerpt: please annotate the pages that mention region isolation / KMS control so our reviewer can find them quickly.

We don't need notarization at this stage; a signed letter from your Head of Compliance will suffice if you can provide it within two business days.

Thanks again — will loop back after the reviewer scan.

Best,
Lena
